data.name: Ayisha
data.gender_notes: Ayisha is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who is a mother to many or a joyful one. The name Ayisha carries the meaning “Life-giving, mother, or joyful” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, English. Parents who choose Ayisha usually hope their child will grow to embody life-giving, mother, or joyful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name of Allah meaning 'the one who is alive-giving or the mother of believers'
data.etymology: Ayisha belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Life-giving, mother, or joyful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayisha total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: عائشة
in_arabic.meaning: تعني عائشة حياة سعيدة وصحية ومليئة بالخير
in_arabic.long_meaning: عائشة هي اسم علم مؤنث مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ع-ي-ش' والذي يعني الحياة السعيدة والمريحة. ورد ذكرها في القرآن الكريم في سورة البقرة، وتدل على الحياة الطيبة والرخاء. في التاريخ الإسلامي، كانت عائشة بنت أبي بكر الصديق زوجة النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهي من أكثر النساء تأثيرًا في التاريخ الإسلامي. يتميز اسم عائشة بكونه رمزًا للحياة السعيدة والمستقرة، ويحمل دلالات روحية عميقة في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: عائشہ
in_urdu.meaning: عائشہ کا مطلب ہے خوشحال زندگی گزارنا
in_urdu.long_meaning: عائشہ ایک عربی نام ہے جو 'ع-ي-ش' جذر سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے آرام دہ اور سعید زندگی۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیا میں مسلمانوں کے درمیان میں بہت مقبول ہے، خاص طور پر پاکستان اور بھارت میں۔ اسلامی روایات میں، عائشہ بنت ابی بکر صدیق نبی محمد صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم کی زوجہ تھیں اور اسلامی تاریخ میں سب سے زیادہ متاثر کن خواتین میں سے ایک ہیں۔

in_hindi.name: आइशा
in_hindi.meaning: आइशा का अर्थ है सुखी और समृद्ध जीवन
in_hindi.long_meaning: आइशा एक अरबी नाम है जो 'ع-ي-ش' मूल से निकला है, जिसका अर्थ है सुखी और समृद्ध जीवन। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत लोकप्रिय है। आइशा का नाम इस्लामी इतिहास में बहुत महत्व रखता है, खासकर हज़रत आइशा बिन्ते अबू बक्र सिद्दीक़ के रूप में, जो नबी मुहम्मद सल्लल्लाहु अलैहि वसल्लम की पत्नी थीं।

in_english.name: Ayisha
in_english.meaning: Ayisha means living, alive, or prosperous life
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ayisha is derived from the Arabic root 'ع-ي-ش' (A-y-sh), which signifies life, living, or a prosperous existence. Referenced in the Quran, Surah Al-Baqarah, it connotes a good and comfortable life. Historically, Ayisha bint Abi Bakr, a wife of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), was a pivotal figure in Islamic history. The name symbolizes a happy and stable life, carrying deep spiritual connotations in Islamic culture. It is widely used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing a life filled with joy and prosperity.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Aisha" holds significant cultural importance in Islamic history, particularly as one of the wives of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). She was a strong, intelligent, and independent woman who played a crucial role in spreading and preserving Islamic knowledge. Her life and teachings have left an indelible mark on Islamic culture, inspiring generations of Muslim women to strive for education, personal growth, and religious observance.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Aisha" also holds deep spiritual significance as it means "one who is a mother to many or a joyful one." This name is a reminder that as Muslim women, we have a role to play in nurturing and raising the next generation of believers, much like the Prophet's beloved wife, Aisha, did. Furthermore, the name encourages us to approach life with a joyful and positive attitude, trusting in Allah's plan and finding pleasure in the journey towards Him.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Life-giving, mother, or joyful" symbolizes The one who is a mother to many or a joyful one. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Ayisha serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of life-giving, mother, or joyful.
